headline_marked: 2 Bangladeshis killed, 4 in ICU after [[Houthi attack on Riyadh airport]]
headline: 2 Bangladeshis killed, 4 in ICU after Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam confirms casualties among Bangladeshis following a deadly strike at King Khalid International Airport.
details: Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed and four others are currently receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of a hospital in Riyadh following an attack at King Khalid International Airport.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam announced the casualties today, stating that the government is working to identify the victims and contact their families.
Bangladesh's missions in Riyadh and Jeddah are coordinating with Saudi authorities to ensure the safety of other Bangladeshi nationals and provide necessary assistance.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment are jointly supporting the victims' families, with the government bearing the costs of repatriating the deceased.
Flights to and from Riyadh have been suspended as a precautionary measure, though no Bangladeshi airlines or flights were reported as directly damaged.
Bangladesh has strongly condemned the Houthi attack on the airport, calling for an immediate end to attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure.
The foreign ministry expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and urged a peaceful resolution of the crisis through dialogue and diplomacy.
caption:
2 Bangladeshis killed and 4 others fighting for their lives in ICU after a deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh airport.

Two Bangladeshi nationals were killed and four others are currently receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of a hospital in Riyadh following an attack at King Khalid International Airport.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam announced the casualties today, stating that the government is working to identify the victims and contact their families.

Bangladesh's missions in Riyadh and Jeddah are coordinating with Saudi authorities to ensure the safety of other Bangladeshi nationals and provide necessary assistance.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment are jointly supporting the victims' families, with the government bearing the costs of repatriating the deceased.

Flights to and from Riyadh have been suspended as a precautionary measure, though no Bangladeshi airlines or flights were reported as directly damaged.

Bangladesh has strongly condemned the Houthi attack on the airport, calling for an immediate end to attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure.

The foreign ministry expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and urged a peaceful resolution of the crisis through dialogue and diplomacy.

headline: Sajek Valley closed indefinitely over security concerns
summary: The Rangamati district administration has banned tourist entry and residence in the popular hill destination until further notice.
details: The Rangamati district administration has temporarily closed the Sajek Valley tourist centre from 6:00pm today until further notice.
The decision was announced in an emergency public notice signed by Rangamati Deputy Commissioner and District Magistrate Nazma Ashrafi.
Tourists currently staying in the area have been ordered to leave Sajek by 5:00pm on October 13 to return safely to their destinations.
The administration cited 'unavoidable reasons' for the sudden closure of the tourist spot in Baghaichhari upazila of Rangamati.
Reports indicate that road blockades have disrupted travel, leaving approximately 2,500 visitors stranded in the area.
caption:
Sajek Valley is shut down. Tourists currently there must leave by October 13.

The Rangamati district administration has temporarily closed the Sajek Valley tourist centre from 6:00pm today until further notice.

The decision was announced in an emergency public notice signed by Rangamati Deputy Commissioner and District Magistrate Nazma Ashrafi.

Tourists currently staying in the area have been ordered to leave Sajek by 5:00pm on October 13 to return safely to their destinations.

The administration cited 'unavoidable reasons' for the sudden closure of the tourist spot in Baghaichhari upazila of Rangamati.

Reports indicate that road blockades have disrupted travel, leaving approximately 2,500 visitors stranded in the area.
